solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Favourable review cheers fool when making cake

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for fried cakes; the clue's singular is used loosely

parts.note: a puff is a piece of uncritical praise or advertising
ta is informal British for thanks
a loon is a silly person
as can mean while or when

explanation.surface: A glowing write-up is toasted when a fool bakes a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: An Australian word found in Chambers; the four short pieces simply join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Australian fried scones or small dough cakes, eaten with jam or syrup.

clue.text: African rhino passes water, raising tail with a shudder at first

definitions.note: rhino is slang for money; pesewas are small coins of Ghana

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a letter moves it up, nearer the top, so the tail letter is lifted inside the word

parts.note: pee means pass water; the tail letter of pees is handled separately
the tail of pees, the third-person form of passes water, is its final S

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: first letter gives S

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros in Africa urinates, shuddering and lifting its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes water' is PEES; 'raising tail' lifts that final S one place up the down entry, giving PESE. Then W ('with'), A, and the S that starts 'shudder' 'at first'. 'rhino' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The pesewa is the hundredth part of the Ghanaian cedi, so pesewas are African money, rhino in slang.

clue.text: Entertaining party, one leaving politician prepared for gathering in theatre

definitions.note: an operation in an operating theatre in which tissue is gathered and stitched

parts.note: fun means entertaining, enjoyable
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged
one letter is leaving the word, taken out of it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lively party from which one politician leaves, ready for a theatre gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is an operating theatre, not a playhouse: fundoplication is surgery that gathers the top of the stomach around the gullet to treat reflux. 'one leaving' leaves POLITCIAN for 'prepared' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundoplication is surgery in which the fundus of the stomach is folded, a plication, around the oesophagus.

clue.text: Historically, one worked hard as male in drag

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to tow is to drag
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: In history a man in women's clothing toiled away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In drag' suggests cross-dressing, but drag is the outer word. Historically flags an Old English term.
explanation.definitionFit: A theow was a slave or bondman in Anglo-Saxon England, someone forced to labour.

clue.text: Stuttering advice to catch hit film

parts.note: a stutter repeats the opening sound of the next word twice
an angler is advised to land a fish, i.e. catch it

explanation.surface: Someone stammers out tips on catching a smash-hit movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter repeats the first syllable of the imperative.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2016 musical starring Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone won six Oscars and earned huge box-office takings.

clue.text: Contact, heading off jet setting once?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its start, and off means removed

parts.note: touch means contact

explanation.surface: Someone touches base before heading off with the jet-set crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet setting' suggests glamorous travel, but jet here is the black gemstone and setting is its mount. Once flags an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ouch was an archaic brooch or clasp in which a jewel such as jet was mounted.

clue.text: Tank owner no longer needing a couple of pints: one is retained

indicators.note: what is retained is held inside, so these letters sit within the others

parts.note: taken as written
a quart is two pints
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish-tank keeper no longer needs a couple of pints, though one is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' looks like part of the story about drinking, but it marks an obsolete spelling, the definition being 'Tank owner no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: This old spelling of aquarist means someone who keeps fish in an aquarium.

clue.text: Nine inspired by Polyhymnia do modulating of medieval scale

indicators.note: what is inspired is breathed in, so it ends up within
to modulate is to shift and vary, so the letters change their order

parts.note: the letters taken as written
IX is Roman nine

explanation.surface: Nine Muses take their cue from Polyhymnia, muse of sacred music, in shifting keys.
explanation.walkthrough: Polyhymnia is one of the nine Muses, so 'Nine' seems to mean the Muses; it is Roman numeral IX.
explanation.definitionFit: In church music this is the plagal mode related to the Mixolydian, one of the medieval modes.

clue.text: Tips for youthful, intriguing debutante turning up so ill at ease

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upward reads the letters bottom to top
the tips of a word are its two ends, so only the end letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of youthful
the first and last letters of intriguing
the first and last letters of debutante

explanation.surface: Advice for a young, fascinating debutante who arrives feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice for the debutante, but it means the ends of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting edgily means acting in a nervous, tense way, uneasy and on edge.

clue.text: Good luck to Hamish's boy, and his niece, taking finals

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: finals are closing letters, so only the ends of the words are used

parts.note: the last letters of his and niece

explanation.surface: Someone wishes Hamish's son and niece well as they sit their final exams.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamish is a stock Scottish name, flagging a Scots word; the apostrophe-s is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots sonse (or sonce) means abundance, prosperity and good fortune.

clue.text: Waited — in shiny coat — years to take part of Romeo

indicators.note: the years letter is to take the role, the part, of the Romeo letter, replacing it

parts.note: lacquered means coated with a glossy varnish
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A varnished actor waited for years to be given the role of Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take part of' means stand in for: Y ('years') takes the place of the R ('Romeo') in LACQUERED. To lackey or lacquey is to wait on someone as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacquey is a footman, so to lacquey is to serve or attend on someone as a menial servant.

clue.text: Bird used to lament audibly

indicators.note: what is audible is heard, so the spelling follows the spoken sound

parts.note: would can mean used to, and to wail is to lament

explanation.surface: A bird that once mourned loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to' reads as a description of the bird's habit, but 'would' expresses habitual past action.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwale is an old name for the green woodpecker or for the golden oriole.

clue.text: Back at home, fine storing gold coins for Balt

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end towards the start

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: something storing goods keeps them inside

parts.note: OK means fine
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Back home, a fine is paid in Baltic gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as OR comes from heraldry. The whole string IN + OORK is read back.
explanation.definitionFit: The kroon was Estonia's currency before the euro; krooni is its plural, money for an Estonian.

clue.text: Cured meat swallowed, choking key judge

indicators.note: to choke something is to grip it round the throat, enclosing it

parts.note: to sink a drink is to swallow it
Alt is a keyboard key
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge chokes on some cured meat he has just swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Key here is a computer key, not a musical one or a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt-junk is a sailors' term for hard, salted beef eaten on long voyages.

clue.text: Early works of Caesar cut without a word from him

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name goes around the Latin word
cut means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: Julian the Apostate was a Roman emperor, holding the title Caesar
veni, I came, is the first word of Julius Caesar's boast veni, vidi, vici

explanation.surface: Caesar's early writings were edited down, leaving out one of his famous words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: JULIA (Julian 'cut') goes round VENI, Caesar's 'I came'.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenilia are the works an author or artist produced while young.

clue.text: A certain cricket jersey in which yours truly's batting for the Irish

definitions.note: Jiminy Cricket is the cricket in Disney's Pinocchio

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one group of letters stands in where the other was

parts.note: Erse is an old name for the Irish Gaelic language
yours truly is the setter, I; I'm in means I am batting

explanation.surface: A cricket jersey that the setter wears to bat for Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: In JERSEY, the letters ERSE ('the Irish') are replaced 'for' IM IN, the setter saying 'I'm in', that is batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiminy Cricket is the talking cricket who acts as Pinocchio's conscience in the Disney film.

clue.text: Sibling having begonia at last in place of Lorraine's fern

indicators.note: a letter put in a word sits inside it

parts.note: bro is short for brother

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of begonia
Metz is the chief city of Lorraine in north-east France

explanation.surface: A sibling grows a begonia where Lorraine's fern used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' reads as a substitution, but 'in' is the insertion and 'place of Lorraine's' is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The barometz or vegetable lamb is a tree fern whose woolly rhizome was once thought to be a plant-animal.

clue.text: Eggs to the left on metal leaving unknown hollow part

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is dropped from the word

parts.note: zinc is a metal
z is an algebraic unknown, here removed

indicators.note: moving leftward in an across entry reads the letters right to left

parts.note: ova are eggs

explanation.surface: Eggs are left on a metal tray, minus an unknown hollow piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the eggs after the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Incavo is the incised, sunken portion of an intaglio carving, its hollowed area.

clue.text: S African leader visiting Greek island, then India

parts.note: someone visiting is in a place
Kos is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A South African leader visits a Greek island and then India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' looks like part of the travel story but supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkosi is the Zulu word for a chief or king, a traditional ruler in South Africa.

clue.text: Old chemist having vehicle not working on Thursday

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece set on another comes after it

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
Th is the abbreviation for Thursday
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: An elderly chemist whose van has broken down on Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the name is ignored in the grid; the order of the last two pieces is set by 'on', not by the clue's word order.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobus van 't Hoff, a Dutch chemist, won the first Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901.

clue.text: Lighter form of transport got on by two little girls

parts.note: Fi and Di are short girls' names
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Two small girls board a lighter means of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter form of transport' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Lighter'. In a down clue 'got on by' puts the girls on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidibus is a paper spill used for lighting a pipe or candle, so it is a lighter.

clue.text: One can put in weight, risking something bouncing?

indicators.note: what is put in something is placed inside it

parts.note: kg is the symbol for kilogram
Roman numeral one
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone gains weight and risks something bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncing' suggests a body or ball; it is a cheque that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiting is writing cheques against funds not yet in the account, which may well be returned unpaid.

clue.text: Sees body badly, having a squint

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sees a body poorly because of a squint.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links poor sight and the squint so neatly that the anagram is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed is British informal for cross-eyed or squinting, with one eye turned.

clue.text: On the way up, buttonhole second person to help with computer?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going upward reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: a buttonhole is a small posy of flowers
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A rising employee collars a deputy to help out with the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttonhole looks like a verb meaning to waylay someone; it is the flower worn in a lapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop is a system operator who runs a computer system or bulletin board.

clue.text: Dye producers team up, turning article black on the outside

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom
turning round puts the letters in the opposite order
being on the outside means wrapping round the middle

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
B is the pencil grading for black
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI

explanation.surface: Dyers form a team, putting black around an item.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the eleven and the pair A, B are turned before the pair goes round the eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Bixa is the annatto tree genus, whose seeds yield an orange-red colouring for food and fabric.

clue.text: Whale is so out of place in large groups of fish

indicators.note: things out of place are disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A whale is clearly out of place among great shoals of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whale, apparently the lone mammal among fish, is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoalwise is an adverb meaning in the manner of a shoal, massed together as fish swim.

clue.text: Measure of brightness that would be reversed by degrees

indicators.note: something reversed runs backwards, last letter first
by can mean within or among, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: BS is the plural of B.S., Bachelor of Science degrees
a would-be driver is a learner, marked L
it can stand for that

explanation.surface: A unit of brightness that would flip gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' looks like 'gradually', but 'by' is an insertion signal and degrees are university qualifications. 'Would be' as L relies on the learner driver's L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The stilb is a unit of luminance, one candela per square centimetre.

clue.text: Shoot back across lounge briefly with, say, 2 social workers' bags

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, wrapped around
going back means reading the letters from the end

parts.note: to zap is to shoot

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to laze is to lounge
2-down is a surgical operation, an op for short; say marks it as an example
ants are social insects and workers

explanation.surface: Someone fires back across a lounge at social workers' handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: Bags looks like handbags but is slang for trousers. Social workers are ants, not caseworkers; the 2 refers to the answer at 2-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is British slang for loose trousers, and palazzo pants are very wide-legged trousers.
